title: From Retrieval to Recognition: Knowledge-Enhanced Post-training of Time Series Foundation Models for Classification
claim: Existing methods discard the source knowledge after pretraining and rely on parameter tuning; ours retrieves and reuses it explicitly alongside the model.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, (a) pretraining context then (b) existing vs (c) ours
description: Three side-by-side panels separated by gray vertical lines. Panel (a) is a gray rounded box of multi-domain class patterns, with small domain icons and red-highlighted waveforms. They feed a pre-training dataset or knowledge base, then a pink pre-training TSFM block, then a blue frozen pre-trained TSFM. A legend marks trainable (flame) and frozen (snowflake). Panel (b), the existing method, has an input time-series curve going down into a yellow dashed fine-tuning box with a TSFM and classification loss. The knowledge base sits off to the side, with a dashed black arrow, a red X and the label 'Discard'. Panel (c) is the same layout, but an orange query encoder and a retriever pull from the knowledge base. Red arrows carry the retrieved patterns into fine-tuning, and a red check mark labels them 'Reused'. The eye goes first to the red marks and arrows.
caption: Illustration of knowledge paradigms in TSFMs for classification. (a) Knowledge learning: TSFMs learn discriminative class patterns from multi-domain pretraining data, storing knowledge implicitly in model parameters. (b) Knowledge transfer: Existing methods adapt this knowledge to target tasks via parameter fine-tuning, without explicitly reusing pretraining data knowledge. (c) Knowledge enhancement: R2R enhances parameter transfer with feature-level retrieval, explicitly leveraging numerical patterns from a pretraining knowledge base to boost recognition. Stage (a) is pretraining; (b) and (c) are post-training, and this work targets the (b)$\rightarrow$(c) transition.
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) have achieved notable progress in classification tasks through large-scale pretraining. However, their post-training practice mainly focuses on implicit parameter fine-tuning, where task-relevant information is entangled with abundant irrelevant knowledge in vast parameter spaces. This may hinder TSFMs from precisely activating useful knowledge for downstream classification. To this end, we propose Retrieval-to-Recognition (R2R), a plug-and-play post-training paradigm that adapts pretrained TSFMs to time series classification. Rather than pretraining a new foundation model, R2R improves how existing TSFMs are post-trained: it introduces a decoupled query encoder to extract discriminative patterns and retrieve instance-level numerical knowledge from a constructed knowledge base. The retrieved explicit knowledge is then fused with the TSFM's implicit parametric embeddings, enabling joint knowledge transfer at both the parameter and feature levels. In this way, R2R allows TSFMs to recall task-relevant patterns learned during pretraining, improving the efficiency of knowledge utilization in downstream classification transfer. Experiments on 158 time series datasets show that R2R consistently improves the classification performance of state-of-the-art TSFMs. Ablation and knowledge-enhanced studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
